description: Evaluates whether an application for the execution of a decree is barred by the maximum 12-year limitation period by determining the precise date the decree became legally enforceable or by classifying the application as a continuation of a previously stayed proceeding rather than a fresh application.
application_scenario: Use when a judgment-debtor challenges an execution application filed more than 12 years after the original decree date, and the decree-holder argues that the limitation period runs from a later date of enforceability (due to statutory stays, amendments, or fulfillment of conditions) or that the application merely revives a closed proceeding.
reasoning_flow: Identify the date of the original decree and the date the current execution application was filed to calculate the elapsed time.
Examine the terms of the decree, any intervening statutory bars, or subsequent appellate/amendment orders to pinpoint the exact moment the decree became legally capable of being enforced.

Assess whether the current application is a 'fresh application' subject to the 12-year bar, or merely a continuation/revival of a previous execution proceeding that was suspended or closed for administrative reasons.
Calculate the 12-year limitation period from the established date of enforceability, excluding any periods of statutory suspension, and conclude whether the execution application is time-barred.
example_application: A decree is passed in 1973, but its execution is statutorily stayed until the decree is scaled down and amended in 1979. The decree-holder files for execution in 1989. The court calculates the 12-year limitation from the 1979 amendment date when the decree became enforceable, holding the application within time.
shared_pattern: All these cases involve the application of the maximum 12-year limitation period for execution (under Section 48 CPC or Article 136 of the Limitation Act) and require determining either the exact date the decree became enforceable or whether the application is a fresh one.
scope_exclusions: Do not use for determining the limitation period for filing initial suits or regular appeals. Do not use for decrees granting a perpetual injunction, which have no limitation period.

description: Evaluates the liability of a mortgagee in possession to pay mesne profits to the mortgagor for the period following the complete discharge of the mortgage debt, distinguishing it from the statutory obligation to render accounts during the subsistence of the mortgage.
application_scenario: Use when a mortgagor seeks to recover profits or damages from a mortgagee who has retained possession of the mortgaged property after the mortgage debt has been fully satisfied by payment, deposit, or statutory discharge.
reasoning_flow: Verify that the property is subject to a mortgage with possession (such as a usufructuary mortgage) and that the mortgagee currently retains or retained possession.

Determine the precise date or event when the principal mortgage debt was completely discharged, whether through actual payment, deposit of redemption money, or operation of a statutory debt relief act.
Classify the nature of the mortgagee's possession post-discharge, recognizing that once the debt is satisfied, the legal right to retain possession extinguishes and the possession becomes wrongful.

Conclude that for the period following the discharge, the mortgagee is liable to pay mesne profits to the mortgagor for unlawful retention of the property, rather than merely rendering accounts under the mortgage terms.
example_application: A usufructuary mortgage debt is statutorily discharged under a Debt Relief Act, but the mortgagee continues in possession. The mortgagor sues for redemption and accounts. The court holds that upon discharge, the mortgagee's possession became wrongful, entitling the mortgagor to mesne profits from the date of discharge rather than a rendition of accounts.
shared_pattern: All these cases address the shift in the nature of a mortgagee's possession from lawful to wrongful upon the complete discharge of the mortgage debt, thereby transforming their liability from rendition of accounts to payment of mesne profits.
scope_exclusions: Do not use for calculating the statutory accounting of rents and profits received by the mortgagee during the active subsistence of the mortgage before the debt is fully discharged.
